what: Wipro is an Indian information technology services company. It runs and modernises the software systems of large corporations, and provides consulting and engineering services, with most delivery staff in India.
customers: Banks, insurers, healthcare companies, manufacturers, retailers and energy companies, mostly in North America and Europe.
money: technology services to US and Canadian clients
Asia Pacific, Middle East and Africa
moat: A trained workforce at Indian cost levels and multi-year contracts embedded in clients' core systems, though it has grown more slowly than its Indian peers.
risks: Revenue fell about 5% last year and has been flat over three years
It has lagged Infosys and TCS in growth for several years
Artificial intelligence could reduce the number of people needed per project
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: A dividend yield above 4% with cash of $4.2 billion against $2.3 billion of debt
Large deal bookings have improved under new leadership
Companies rebuilding systems around artificial intelligence need this kind of implementation work
watch: Revenue growth in constant currency and large deal wins.
